tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit (independent WebSearch/WebFetch re-verification): CORRECTED a hallucination carried from the prior pass — the markdown attributed a 'brown grouper population of ~200 individuals' to La Gabiniere. Cross-checked against miopalmoplongee.com (direct fetch), vacances-plongee.fr and plongeur.com: the ~200 figure is documented as a BARRACUDA school (present since summer 2001, 10-20m), not groupers. Grouper counts are independently described as 'not rare to see about ten in a single dive' / 'the largest concentration of brown grouper in the western Mediterranean' — no numeric population estimate exists in sources. Markdown corrected accordingly. Zones (Tombant Est/Ouest, Calanque Sombre, Dolmen at 33-35m) confirmed via miopalmoplongee.com.

2026-08-24 re-audit: depth and monkfish (baudroie) claim re-confirmed via independent WebSearch of nicoblon.free.fr, which specifies the monkfish is found 'sur le sable' at approximately 28m on the eastern side — consistent with, and more precise than, the prior 'east face rocky bottom' description. Markdown updated with the 28m detail. Depth corrected to 35m (Aqualonde confirms 35m max; previous value 34m was rounding). Giant doris and largest-scorpionfish-in-Port-Cros claims remain sourced to miopalmoplongee.com only (single-source, kept as attributed operator claim rather than fact).

2026-08-24 re-audit: directly refetched fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donator, ulysseplongee.fr/blog/le-donator, and en.bormesplongee.fr/donator. Three-way casualty conflict CONFIRMED (not resolved): fr.wikipedia.org states 'le naufrage fera tout de meme 5 morts' (5 deaths); ulysseplongee.fr states 'trois victimes seront denombrees' (3 victims); en.bormesplongee.fr states 2 of 29 crew went missing, 27 rescued (0 confirmed deaths). Depth also varies across sources: deck cited as low as 35m and as deep as 44m; propeller/stern cited between 48m and 52m. Both conflicts written into markdown per anti-hallucination policy rather than picking one figure. Build data reconfirmed unchanged: 78.28m x 11.94m, 1698 GRT, Bergen Mekaniske Verksted 1931, mine strike 10 Nov 1945 13:15, sank in under 4 minutes.

tags.description: Classic Mediterranean wall dive with vertical drop, 10-38m. Posidonia seagrass meadows on shallow plateau. Groupers, catsharks, moray eels, and white gorgonians. Excellent macro photography and light penetration. 15m+ visibility typical.
tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit: independent WebSearch of miopalmoplongee.com's Pointe Vaisseau page confirms groupers (fewer than La Gabiniere but large specimens), small-spotted catsharks resting under rocks, moray eels, spiny lobsters, and white gorgonians. Site area given as ~9000 sq m to 38m depth by one source (vs. prior 35m) — depth range widened to 10-38m to reflect this. Amberjacks were not confirmed by any source consulted and have been removed from the marine life list.

2026-08-24 re-audit: located and fetched a dedicated French Wikipedia article, fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagona_(epave), specific to this Mediterranean wreck (distinct from the English-language SS Sagona article about the vessel's earlier Newfoundland ferry service). It independently corroborates every core fact: built 1912, Dundee Shipbuilding Co., 53.3m x 8.6m, 808 tons, struck a mine to port and sank immediately on 3 December 1945, 2 dead + 1 missing, wreck lies 35-47m between Port-Cros and Porquerolles. This resolves prior uncertainty about the English Wikipedia SS Sagona article's mismatched 21 November date — that article covers the ship's Newfoundland career and gives a less precise/likely erroneous loss date; the dedicated French wreck article and all dive-specific sources agree on 3 December. Added fr.wikipedia.org as a validation source.

2026-08-24 re-audit: independent WebSearch cross-check of tribloo.com and provencemed.com confirms white gorgonian colony (described as 'immense', alongside sponges), groupers, sar/wrasse schools, moray eels, and barbiers; topography (ridge to 30m sand, second ridge further west at 50-70m) matches prior description. Exposure to easterly wind and frequent current confirmed. No changes to site_type/depth/difficulty needed.

tags.description: Shore-accessible reef in protected marine reserve with snorkeling trail (6 buoys), 1-12m. Beginner-friendly posidonia seagrass exploration. Groupers, bream, and nudibranchs common. Excellent for learning Mediterranean reef ecology.
tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit: official park source (portcros-parcnational.fr) and CaPel re-confirmed as live, accurate references for the marked underwater trail and reserve-effect fish habituation. No factual changes required.

No site-specific sources found in QA passes 2026-05-25, 2026-06-26, or 2026-08-24 (this pass repeated WebSearch in French and English, no new results). The confirmed 'Les Deux Frères' is a distinct rock formation at Cap Sicié near La Seyne-sur-Mer, over 30km from Port-Cros, where divers visit the wreck of the tanker Arroyo (sunk 1953) — unrelated to this destination. No Port-Cros operator lists a 'Les Deux Frères' site. Remains unvalidated; regional characteristics only, not marked validated.

The confirmed site near Bagaud island is 'Les Dalles de Bagaud' / 'Dalles de Bagaud' (west side at Pointe du Beau, >10,000 sq m, 6-12m, beginner) — re-confirmed 2026-08-24 via destination.portcros-parcnational.fr and divingiens.fr. No source found for a site named 'Pierre de Bagaud' at 25m in this or the prior two passes (2026-05-25, 2026-06-26). These are likely distinct features. Do not mark validated until operator-specific source confirms this exact name and depth.
tags.description: Bagaud island reef (pierre = rock) with rocky formations and posidonia, 5-25m. Intermediate exploration of marine reserve with groupers, octopus, and sea fans. Good visibility (20m+) and moderate currents.

tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit: none of the three cited sources, nor further WebSearch, independently name or describe a distinct 'Gabiniere Nord' dive site — all describe La Gabiniere islet as a whole (Tombant Est/Ouest, Calanque Sombre, Dolmen) with no published 'north face' characterization. This entry corresponds to a separate OSM mooring/access node on the north side of the same islet, not a separately documented operator site. Markdown revised to make this explicit and to remove invented comparative claims (previously stated the north side has 'fewer groupers than the south's ~200' — the 200 figure itself was a hallucination, see La Gabiniere qa_note). Kept validated=true because the underlying fauna/flora claims are grounded in confirmed general-Gabiniere sourcing and the site is physically the same feature, but comparative specifics beyond that are no longer asserted.
2026-08-24 re-audit: official park and CaPel sources re-confirmed live and consistent with description. No factual changes required.
tags.description: Beach dive site (plage = beach) with easy shore access, depths 2-8m. Beginner-friendly Mediterranean reef with posidonia seagrass beds. Less crowded than La Palud with comparable marine richness.

tags.qa_note: Site exists as a geographic point on Port-Cros and, per 2026-08-24 re-check, is named specifically in the park's own diving regulations as one boundary of the zone where night diving is authorised (between Pointe du Cognet and Pointe de Port-Man, max 20 divers, park notified before 19:00) — confirming this is a real, recognised location, not a fabricated name. However no dive operator publishes site-specific depth, site type, or marine life details for it, so it is still NOT marked validated per the 3+ distinct source requirement.
tags.description: Point (pointe) reef with deeper exploration, 8-30m. Intermediate Mediterranean dive with rocky formations, groupers, and amberjacks. Posidonia and macroalgae. Visibility typically 15-25m with light currents.

tags.name: La Tantine
tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit: independent WebSearch re-confirms every core fact — small wooden vessel 15-20m x 6m, no engine/propeller, sank c.1960 during a tow while carrying construction materials (single-row bricks, motorised pump) for Port-Cros's Manoir hotel, crane rising 3-4m above the sand, located off Bagaud's north point, ~48m depth (range 41-49m across sources), conger eel population reduced from a large 1990s population to 2-3 individuals today. Note: sources remain internally contradictory on vessel classification — some (e.g. one general summary) still call it a 'tugboat with a rear crane' despite explicitly stating it had no motor, which is why the markdown describes it as an unpowered crane barge/ponton grue while noting the 'tugboat' label appears in some sources. No changes to depth/type/difficulty.

tags.name: Wildcat
tags.qa_note: 2026-08-24 re-audit: directly refetched en.bormesplongee.fr/wildcat and cross-checked against a further independent WebSearch (aquabormes.fr-family content). Origin remains genuinely disputed between two sources: deliberate 1950s jettison from a carrier (tentatively HMS Hermes, damage-related) vs. an operational crash/ditching; retracted gear favours the crash theory per bormesplongee.fr's own reasoning, creating an internal tension in that source worth flagging rather than resolving. Machine gun count: aircraft-type spec (F4F/Martlet) is 6 guns total per bormesplongee.fr's general description; however an independently found site-specific description states '2 mitrailleuses toujours en place dans chacune des ailes' (2 still in place in each wing = 4 visible on the wreck) — this is DIFFERENT information (visible-on-wreck count) from the historical full-armament spec (6), not a contradiction of it. Markdown revised to distinguish 'as-built armament' (6 guns, historical spec) from 'as found on the wreck' (4 visible, per site-specific source) rather than presenting a single number. Depth range widened slightly to 51-54m to reflect a source giving 54m.
